Send a message seven bits to a byte, each byte ending in a parity bit that makes its count of ones even, and decode a transmission back, rejecting a byte whose parity is wrong.

<a class="nomi-rough-badge" href="#rough-edges">rough edges</a> Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/intergalactic-transmission) (MIT). Listed under [Encoding & Ciphers](/examples/?subject=encoding-and-ciphers).

```nomi-run
// FILE: intergalactic_transmission.nomi
/// The bytes that carry `message`: its bits seven at a time, the last seven
/// padded with zeros, each followed by a parity bit that makes the byte's
/// count of ones even.
//! assert transmit([0x05]) == [0x05, 0x81]
//
pub fn transmit(message: List<Int>) -> List<Int> {
    message
    |> Iter.flat_map(bits)
    |> Iter.chunks(7)
    |> Iter.map(fn chunk -> {
        data = Int.shift_left(from_bits(chunk), 7 - Iter.count(chunk))
        Int.shift_left(data, 1) + Iter.sum(chunk) % 2
    })
    |> Iter.to_list()
}

/// The message `transmission` carries: the seven data bits of each byte,
/// eight at a time, with the bits left over at the end dropped. A byte whose
/// count of ones is odd was damaged on the way, and is `Err("wrong parity")`.
//! assert receive([0x05, 0x81]) == Ok([0x05])
//
pub fn receive(transmission: List<Int>) -> Result<List<Int>, String> {
    data =
        transmission
        |> Iter.map(data_bits)
        |> try Result.collect()

    data
    |> Iter.flatten()
    |> Iter.chunks(8)
    |> Iter.filter(&(Iter.count(&1) == 8))
    |> Iter.map(from_bits)
    |> Iter.to_list()
    |> Ok()
}

/// The first seven bits of `byte`, or an error when its parity is odd.
fn data_bits(byte: Int) -> Result<List<Int>, String> {
    all = Iter.to_list(bits(byte))

    if Iter.sum(all) % 2 == 0 {
        all |> Iter.take(7) |> Iter.to_list() |> Ok()
    } else {
        Err("wrong parity")
    }
}

/// The eight bits of `byte`, most significant first.
fn bits(byte: Int) -> Iter<Int> {
    Iter.map(0..8, fn i -> Int.bitwise_and(Int.shift_right(byte, 7 - i), 1))
}

/// The number whose bits, most significant first, are `bits`.
fn from_bits(bits: List<Int>) -> Int {
    Iter.reduce(bits, fn n = 0, bit -> n * 2 + bit)
}

// FILE: intergalactic_transmission_test.nomi
import intergalactic_transmission.{receive, transmit}

test "calculate transmit sequences" {
    cases = [
        #("empty message", [], []),
        #("0x00 is transmitted as 0x0000", [0x00], [0x00, 0x00]),
        #("0x02 is transmitted as 0x0300", [0x02], [0x03, 0x00]),
        #("0x06 is transmitted as 0x0600", [0x06], [0x06, 0x00]),
        #("0x05 is transmitted as 0x0581", [0x05], [0x05, 0x81]),
        #("0x29 is transmitted as 0x2881", [0x29], [0x28, 0x81]),
        #(
            "0xc001c0de is transmitted as 0xc000711be1",
            [0xC0, 0x01, 0xC0, 0xDE],
            [0xC0, 0x00, 0x71, 0x1B, 0xE1],
        ),
        #(
            "six byte message",
            [0x47, 0x72, 0x65, 0x61, 0x74, 0x21],
            [0x47, 0xB8, 0x99, 0xAC, 0x17, 0xA0, 0x84],
        ),
        #(
            "seven byte message",
            [0x47, 0x72, 0x65, 0x61, 0x74, 0x31, 0x21],
            [0x47, 0xB8, 0x99, 0xAC, 0x17, 0xA0, 0xC5, 0x42],
        ),
        #(
            "eight byte message",
            [0xC0, 0x01, 0x13, 0x37, 0xC0, 0xDE, 0x21, 0x21],
            [0xC0, 0x00, 0x44, 0x66, 0x7D, 0x06, 0x78, 0x42, 0x21, 0x81],
        ),
        #(
            "twenty byte message",
            [
                0x45, 0x78, 0x65, 0x72, 0x63, 0x69, 0x73, 0x6D, 0x20, 0x69, 0x73, 0x20, 0x61, 0x77,
                0x65, 0x73, 0x6F, 0x6D, 0x65, 0x21,
            ],
            [
                0x44, 0xBD, 0x18, 0xAF, 0x27, 0x1B, 0xA5, 0xE7, 0x6C, 0x90, 0x1B, 0x2E, 0x33, 0x03,
                0x84, 0xEE, 0x65, 0xB8, 0xDB, 0xED, 0xD7, 0x28, 0x84,
            ],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, message, expected), description {
        assert transmit(message) == expected
    }
}

test "decode received messages" {
    cases = [
        #("empty message", [], Ok([])),
        #("zero message", [0x00, 0x00], Ok([0x00])),
        #("0x0300 is decoded to 0x02", [0x03, 0x00], Ok([0x02])),
        #("0x0581 is decoded to 0x05", [0x05, 0x81], Ok([0x05])),
        #("0x2881 is decoded to 0x29", [0x28, 0x81], Ok([0x29])),
        #("first byte has wrong parity", [0x07, 0x00], Err("wrong parity")),
        #("second byte has wrong parity", [0x03, 0x68], Err("wrong parity")),
        #("0xcf4b00 is decoded to 0xce94", [0xCF, 0x4B, 0x00], Ok([0xCE, 0x94])),
        #("0xe2566500 is decoded to 0xe2ad90", [0xE2, 0x56, 0x65, 0x00], Ok([0xE2, 0xAD, 0x90])),
        #(
            "six byte message",
            [0x47, 0xB8, 0x99, 0xAC, 0x17, 0xA0, 0x84],
            Ok([0x47, 0x72, 0x65, 0x61, 0x74, 0x21]),
        ),
        #(
            "seven byte message",
            [0x47, 0xB8, 0x99, 0xAC, 0x17, 0xA0, 0xC5, 0x42],
            Ok([0x47, 0x72, 0x65, 0x61, 0x74, 0x31, 0x21]),
        ),
        #(
            "last byte has wrong parity",
            [0x47, 0xB8, 0x99, 0xAC, 0x17, 0xA0, 0xC5, 0x43],
            Err("wrong parity"),
        ),
        #(
            "eight byte message",
            [0xC0, 0x00, 0x44, 0x66, 0x7D, 0x06, 0x78, 0x42, 0x21, 0x81],
            Ok([0xC0, 0x01, 0x13, 0x37, 0xC0, 0xDE, 0x21, 0x21]),
        ),
        #(
            "twenty byte message",
            [
                0x44, 0xBD, 0x18, 0xAF, 0x27, 0x1B, 0xA5, 0xE7, 0x6C, 0x90, 0x1B, 0x2E, 0x33, 0x03,
                0x84, 0xEE, 0x65, 0xB8, 0xDB, 0xED, 0xD7, 0x28, 0x84,
            ],
            Ok([
                0x45, 0x78, 0x65, 0x72, 0x63, 0x69, 0x73, 0x6D, 0x20, 0x69, 0x73, 0x20, 0x61, 0x77,
                0x65, 0x73, 0x6F, 0x6D, 0x65, 0x21,
            ]),
        ),
        #(
            "wrong parity on 16th byte",
            [
                0x44, 0xBD, 0x18, 0xAF, 0x27, 0x1B, 0xA5, 0xE7, 0x6C, 0x90, 0x1B, 0x2E, 0x33, 0x03,
                0x84, 0xEF, 0x65, 0xB8, 0xDB, 0xED, 0xD7, 0x28, 0x84,
            ],
            Err("wrong parity"),
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, transmission, expected), description {
        assert receive(transmission) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Both directions work on a stream of bits rather than shifting a carry between bytes: `bits` answers a byte's eight bits most significant first, and `from_bits` folds a list of bits back into a number. `transmit` is `Iter.flat_map(bits)`, `Iter.chunks(7)` and one byte per chunk; `receive` checks and strips each byte, `Iter.flatten`s the data bits and reads them back eight at a time.
- The last chunk of a message may be short. `transmit` shifts it left by what it lacks, which pads it with zeros, and its parity is the sum of its bits modulo 2, so padding needs no special case. `receive` drops a short last chunk, the padding the sender added.
- A byte with odd parity is `Err("wrong parity")`, the canonical message, as grains and variable-length-quantity do with their one error. `Result.collect` stops at the first bad byte.
- Bytes are `List<Int>` written in hex, as in variable-length-quantity, for the reason its Friction gives.
- The transmit and decode groups are one `subtests` table each, named by the description column.

## Rough edges

Where Nomi made this exercise harder than it should be. Each is an open question for the language, not a settled answer.

- **Longer than it should be.** There are no bitwise operators, so reading bit `i` of a byte is `Int.bitwise_and(Int.shift_right(byte, 7 - i), 1)` and making room for the parity bit `Int.shift_left(data, 1)`, where Rust, Go and Python write `byte >> (7 - i) & 1` and `data << 1`.
